title: Introduce intake-lite manifest, weighted performance stamps, and release-teaser composer
author: Maya Chen
release_notes: Adds an opt-in lightweight intake manifest and automated release teaser composer; introduces a compact weighted performance stamping scheme to seed changelog snippets and onboarding heuristics. No breaking changes.
short_summary: Opt-in lightweight manifest with perf-stamps for faster model intake and an automated short release teaser generator to improve changelog drafts.
body:
Motivation: the current model intake flow produces verbose manifests and large perf-profile payloads that slow down iterative onboarding for small models and experimental variants. This PR introduces an opt-in 'intake-lite' manifest format (smaller schema, sampled telemetry pointers) and a compact 'weighted performance stamp' that summarizes latency/throughput/quality signals used to seed human-readable release-teasers. The release-teaser composer aggregates those stamps and the model's short metadata to auto-draft a one-paragraph release note aimed at product/marketing reviewers.

What changed (single continuous description): added a lightweight manifest schema (intake_lite.yaml) and parser, a perf-stamp generator that reduces perf profile size by summarizing key percentiles and a normalized weight for each signal, a teaser composer that turns stamps+metadata into a short release-blurb, minor console display hooks to preview the teaser in the onboarding UI, and unit and integration tests. The lightweight manifest is explicitly opt-in (onboard flow flag or CLI switch) and coexists with the full manifest, with a shim in the intake path to expand lite-manifests into a compact internal representation for downstream tools.

Design notes: weighted performance stamps are intentionally lossy but designed to be bias-corrected: each stamp includes a confidence weight computed from sample count and variance; downstream algorithms can de-noise with sampling metadata. The teaser composer is a templated, non-ML generator with short, editable templates per team so it does not auto-publish without human review.

Rollout plan: feature gated behind 'intake_lite' flag. We will enable the flag for opt-in teams and one internal pilot for two weeks, collect telemetry on intake latency, manifest size, and reviewer upstream edits to teasers. After pilot validation, flip default to enable lightweight intake for models under 200MB and with fewer than 50 sample traces.

Testing and CI: added unit tests covering manifest parsing, stamp generation, and teaser templates; added integration tests for the intake shim and e2e onboarding flow in the test harness. CI currently green on this branch.

Operator notes: operators will see a small new file under registry/intake/ and a preview pane in the console. No DB migrations required. Admins may toggle the intake_lite flag via the feature flags UI or the admin API.

Checklist: [x] schema + parser added, [x] perf-stamp algorithm implemented, [x] teaser composer implemented, [x] console preview hook, [x] unit/integration tests, [x] docs and onboarding guide, [x] pilot rollout plan documented.

Related work: builds on prior perf-sampler work (ENG-612) and ties into the changelog drafting efforts in PM-123.

Compatibility: backward compatible with existing pipelines; the shim expands lite manifests where full manifests are expected.

review_comments: Rafael Ortega: Nice approach — can you clarify how confidence weights are computed? (requested change)
Maya Chen: replied — weights are sqrt(N)/(1+variance) scaled to [0,1]; added inline doc and unit test to validate edge cases.
